interpretation.interpretation: One client WebSocket closed during exercise. The remaining completed rounds are descriptive only; this run does not qualify for capacity guidance. The sampled server process retained one instance ID, but this does not identify which layer closed that WebSocket. Only one user was sampled in detail, and it was not the affected user. No cause or saturation threshold is inferred. Heavier comparable loads are not scheduled after this failure.

cloudLogQuery.interpretation: The query returned startup, migration, and shutdown INFO records around the planned 14:30 schema transition. It returned no record explaining either socket closure. Session logging was disabled, so absence of an error record does not exclude a server error.

interpretation.clientDiagnosticLimitation: Pinned Serverpod client 4f2a75a emits WebSocketClosedException when its socket stream finishes. interpretation.finding: XXL Person at 128 participating devices converged, but needed 540.65 seconds for 300 seconds of offered traffic (17.76 rather than 32 rounds/s). One statement in conflict/reference planning accounts for 2186.56 ms of 2376.97 ms sampled merge SQL wall time. Connection and begin averaged 7.42 ms; global merge-capacity waiting averaged 4.50 ms.

sourceLead.detail: The projection fast path batches dependency checks into one SELECT. The source includes reverse-reference NOT EXISTS probes on child tables, currently without a spaceId predicate. This is a query-plan investigation lead; no EXPLAIN plan was captured for this workload.

interpretation.limits: One sampled user. The XL comparison has a different population and tier, so it is descriptive, not an isolated speedup or a hardware comparison. SQL wall time includes server scheduling, driver and network waits and PostgreSQL execution; it does not prove sequential scans, CPU saturation, lock contention, or a database-location cause.
interpretation.sizingConsequence: Do not qualify the 128-device Person short-screen result as sustained capacity. Final candidate validation must refine downward after a sustained failure rather than recommend that failed boundary.
